name: hypoxia-motility
title: Hypoxia → motility (grammar on a reference substrate)
question: Does the generic grammar engine, driven by the paper's verbatim hypoxia rules, reproduce the transient post-hypoxic motile phenotype on a minimal reference ABM?
hypothesis: Executing the PhysiCell hypoxia rules (oxygen decreases transform-to-motile and necrosis; pressure decreases cycling) through viva_grammar on an oxygen-field + point-agent substrate yields a hypoxic core that induces a migratory phenotype, an invasive plume, a central necrotic core, and reversion on reoxygenation.
objective: Demonstrate end-to-end that viva_grammar.composites.hypoxia.hypoxia_motility reproduces the paper's qualitative hypoxia dynamics, with the grammar engine as a separate, pluggable process (the same role it will play for the MISM blueprint ABMs).
description: The showcase study for viva-grammar. The generic GrammarRulesProcess reads the verbatim hypoxia rules and drives the minimal reference substrate. Oxygen is depleted into a central hypoxic core; core cells transition to a motile phenotype (baseline speed 0.47 µm/min) and migrate up the oxygen gradient; the deepest core goes necrotic; late reoxygenation (uptake relief) reverts the motile cells.

expected_behavior.name: phenotype-induction
expected_behavior.en: Low oxygen induces a motile phenotype — peak motile-cell fraction reaches at least 0.15.
expected_behavior.rationale: "oxygen decreases transform to motile tumor": as the core becomes hypoxic the transition rate rises, producing motile cells (baseline fraction is exactly 0).

expected_behavior.name: invasive-plume
expected_behavior.en: Motile cells migrate outward — at the motile peak their mean radius is ≥ 1.2× the non-motile mean.
expected_behavior.rationale: Motile cells do a biased walk up the oxygen gradient, forming an invasive plume.

expected_behavior.name: transience-reversion
expected_behavior.en: On reoxygenation the phenotype reverts — motile fraction falls to ≤ 0.02.
expected_behavior.rationale: "oxygen increases transform to tumor": restored oxygen reverts motile cells.

expected_behavior.name: necrotic-core
expected_behavior.en: Necrosis is confined to the core — mean necrotic radius stays below the mean live radius.
expected_behavior.rationale: "oxygen decreases necrosis": only the anoxic center necroses.

behavior_tests.name: invasive-plume
behavior_tests.description: Mean motile radius ≥ 1.2× mean non-motile radius at the motile peak (observed ≈ 1.40×).

behavior_tests.name: necrotic-core
behavior_tests.description: Mean necrotic radius < mean live radius throughout (central core).

visualizations.name: hypoxia-motility-spatial-dynamics
visualizations.title: Oxygen field, cell cohort, and dynamics over time

conclusion: PASS on all four acceptance bands. The grammar engine reproduces the paper's transient post-hypoxic migration: peak motile fraction ≈ 0.34, invasive-plume ratio ≈ 1.40×, reversion to 0.00 after reoxygenation, and a central necrotic core throughout — with the grammar running as a separate, ABM-agnostic process.
